context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is an enterprise platform designed for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Patrons / Library Members (Person)
* Librarians / Staff (Person)
* Library Management System (Software System)
* External Payment Gateway (Software System)
* Digital Content Providers / e-Book Vendors (Software System)
* Notification Service (Software System)
* External Enterprise Search Service (Subsystem)

## Relationships
* Patrons & Librarians -> Library Management System (HTTPS/WSS)
* Library Management System -> External Payment Gateway (REST/TLS)
* Library Management System -> Digital Content Providers (REST/OAuth2)
* Library Management System -> Notification Service (HTTPS/SMTP)

## Technology Stack
* Cloud-native EU Infrastructure: Selected to guarantee compliance with EU-only data residency constraints.
* REST and TLS/HTTPS: Used for secure external integrations and client-server communication.
* OAuth2: Implemented for secure authentication with digital content providers.
* SMTP and HTTPS: Utilized by the Notification Service for automated alerts.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with EU data residency while maintaining high performance, meeting the 800ms search response requirement through dedicated subsystem boundaries. External integrations are securely isolated using standard protocols.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portal capabilities for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and meets strict sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Patrons and Librarians (Users)
- Web Application (React, TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
- Core Business Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Elasticsearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Redis Cache
- Notification Worker (Node.js)
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, e-Book Vendors, Notification Service, Enterprise Search Service

## Relationships
- Web App -> API Gateway via HTTPS/JSON
- API Gateway -> Core Business Service & Search Service via gRPC/REST
- Core Business Service -> Database via TCP
- Core Business Service -> Redis Cache via TCP/RESP
- Core Business Service -> External Payment Gateway via HTTPS
- Notification Worker -> External Notification Service via HTTPS/AMQP

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript: Frontend web application for responsive user interfaces.
- Java, Spring Boot: Robust backend for core cataloguing and circulation business logic.
- Elasticsearch: Dedicated search engine ensuring 99th-percentile search response < 800 ms (R-05).
- PostgreSQL: Primary relational database restricted to EU infrastructure for data residency constraints.
- Redis: In-memory cache to reduce database load during high-traffic browsing.
- Node.js: Asynchronous background worker for decoupled notification processing.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples heavy search operations into Elasticsearch to achieve the sub-800ms performance mandate. Additionally, localizing PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch within EU infrastructure strictly satisfies regional data residency constraints.

Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture ensures EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
- Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff
- Web Application (React, TypeScript) with internal components: Router / Layout (React Router), Authentication (Auth Context / OAuth2 SDK), Catalogue & Search, Circulation & Self-Service
- API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
- Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Elasticsearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL) and Redis Cache (Redis)
- Notification Worker (Node.js)
- External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers, Notification Service, External Enterprise Search Service

## Relationships
- Patrons / Librarians -> Router / Layout: Uses [HTTPS]
- Catalogue & Search Component -> API Gateway: Queries search and catalogue data via [HTTPS/JSON]
- Circulation & Self-Service Component -> API Gateway: Executes transactions via [HTTPS/JSON]
- Web Application -> API Gateway: Sends requests to backend services [HTTPS/JSON]

## Technology Stack
- React and TypeScript: Powers the responsive frontend web application
- React Router: Manages navigation and layouts
- OAuth2 SDK: Handles authentication and role-based access
- React Query / SWR: Implements client-side result caching for performance
- Kong / Nginx: Acts as API Gateway
- Java with Spring Boot: Powers Core Business Service
- Elasticsearch: Provides search capabilities
- PostgreSQL: Stores system data within EU boundaries
- Redis Cache: Accelerates frequently accessed data
- Node.js: Powers Notification Worker
- Localized EU CDN: Serves UI assets for data residency compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses localized EU infrastructure and client-side caching to satisfy strict EU-only data residency constraints. It decouples services to achieve 99th-percentile search responses under 800 ms.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture enforces EU-only data residency while maintaining high-performance search responses under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
- Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff (Users)
- Web Application (React, TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Kong / Nginx) containers: SSL/TLS Termination Component, Authentication & Authorization Component, Routing & Load Balancing Component, Rate Limiting & Throttling Component
- Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Elasticsearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Redis Cache (Redis)
- Notification Worker (Node.js)
- External Systems: External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers / e-Book Vendors, Notification Service, External Enterprise Search Service

## Relationships
- Patrons / Librarians -> SSL/TLS Termination Component: Inbound traffic [HTTPS]
- Web Application -> Authentication & Authorization Component: Validates credentials [HTTPS/JSON]
- SSL/TLS Termination Component -> Authentication & Authorization Component: Passes decrypted requests [Internal]
- Authentication & Authorization Component -> Routing & Load Balancing Component: Forwards validated requests [Internal]
- Routing & Load Balancing Component -> Core Business Service: Forwards authenticated traffic [gRPC]
- Routing & Load Balancing Component -> Search Service: Forwards search queries [gRPC]
- Routing & Load Balancing Component -> Redis Cache: Checks rate limits [RESP/TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Kong / Nginx & Lua: API Gateway core and routing plugins for edge traffic management
- OpenSSL / Nginx: SSL/TLS termination and perimeter security enforcing EU data residency
- Kong JWT Plugin & OAuth2: Edge-based authentication to offload backend services
- Redis: Backs rate limiting and throttling to protect search performance SLAs (R-05)
- Java / Spring Boot: Core Business Service implementation
- Elasticsearch: Dedicated Search Service ensuring low-latency catalog queries (< 800 ms)
- React & TypeScript: Web Application frontend
- PostgreSQL: Persistent data storage within EU boundary

## Rationale
Decomposing the API Gateway isolates edge security, SSL termination, and rate limiting to protect downstream services. This guarantees the 800ms search SLA while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.

Core Business Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portal capabilities for public and academic libraries. It enforces strict EU-only data residency while ensuring high-performance search responses under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
- Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff (Users)
- Web Application (React, TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
- Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot) containing:
  - Catalog Management Component (Spring Data JPA)
  - Circulation Component (Spring Transactions)
  - Payment Integration Component (Spring Cloud OpenFeign)
  - Search Integration Component (Spring WebClient)
- Search Service (Elasticsearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Redis Cache (Redis)
- Notification Worker (Node.js)
- External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers, Notification Service

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Core Business Service: Routes business requests [gRPC/REST]
- Catalog Management Component -> Redis Cache: Caches hot catalog items [TCP/Lettuce]
- Circulation Component -> Database: Persists transaction states [TCP/JDBC]
- Payment Integration Component -> External Payment Gateway: Processes fines [HTTPS/JSON]
- Catalog Management Component -> Search Service: Synchronizes item metadata [HTTP/REST]
- Core Business Service -> Database: Reads and writes persistent data [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Java and Spring Boot: Chosen for robust enterprise backend logic and modular domain-driven design.
- PostgreSQL: Provides reliable relational persistence within EU data residency constraints.
- Elasticsearch: Delivers sub-800ms 99th-percentile search performance for catalog items.
- Redis: Caches frequently accessed data to reduce database load.
- React and TypeScript: Powers the responsive front-end user interface.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a modular Spring Boot monolith backed by specialized caching and search technologies to meet strict performance targets. EU data residency is strictly maintained through localized PostgreSQL deployment and isolated container boundaries.

Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces EU-only data residency while guaranteeing high-performance search responses.

## Key Elements
* Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff (Users)
* Web Application (React, TypeScript)
* API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
* Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot)
* Search API Application (Java, Spring Boot)
* Elasticsearch Cluster (Elasticsearch 8.x)
* Query Cache Layer (Local Caffeine cache)
* Database (PostgreSQL) and Redis Cache (Redis)
* Notification Worker (Node.js)
* External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers, Notification Service, External Enterprise Search Service

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Search API Application: Forwards search requests via `gRPC`
* Search API Application -> Elasticsearch Cluster: Executes queries via `Transport Client over TCP`
* Core Business Service -> Search API Application: Syncs catalogue changes via `JSON over Kafka` events
* Search API Application -> Query Cache Layer: Checks recent search results via `In-memory Java API`

## Technology Stack
* Java with Spring Boot for Search API Application, providing robust backend logic and EU data residency enforcement
* Elasticsearch 8.x for indexing and full-text search capabilities
* Local Caffeine cache for in-memory query caching
* Apache Kafka for asynchronous event-driven catalogue synchronization
* `gRPC` for internal inter-service communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses an isolated Search API Application fronting an Elasticsearch cluster to meet the strict sub-800ms search performance requirement. Asynchronous Kafka synchronization and local caching minimize latency and resource load while maintaining data consistency.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
- Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff (Users)
- External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers, Notification Service, External Enterprise Search Service (External Systems)
- Web Application (React, TypeScript), API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
- Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot), Search Service (Elasticsearch), Notification Worker (Node.js)
- Database (PostgreSQL) and Redis Cache (Redis)
- Database Components: Relational Storage Engine (PostgreSQL 15), Connection Pooler (PgBouncer), Audit Logging Extension (`pgAudit`), Full-Text Search Index (PostgreSQL GIN Indexes)

## Relationships
- Core Business Service -> Connection Pooler (PgBouncer): Database queries and transactions [TCP/SQL via JDBC, port 6432]
- Connection Pooler -> Relational Storage Engine: Proxied client connections [TCP, local socket]
- Relational Storage Engine -> Audit Logging Extension (`pgAudit`): Writes security and data access event logs [Internal PostgreSQL Hook]
- Core Business Service -> Database: Reads and writes persistent data [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL 15: Core relational engine for ACID-compliant storage of patrons, items, and transactions within EU infrastructure
- PgBouncer: Connection pooler to manage concurrent connections and meet performance NFRs
- `pgAudit`: Extension for strict database-level activity logging to satisfy EU compliance
- PostgreSQL GIN Indexes: Native full-text search index for fast metadata filtering

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU data residency compliance while supporting high-performance search and scalable circulation workflows. Component-level isolation via connection pooling and auditing guarantees reliability under load.

Redis Cache.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency while maintaining a 99th-percentile search response under 800ms.

## Key Elements
* Patrons / Library Members and Librarians / Staff (Users)
* Web Application (React, TypeScript)
* API Gateway (Kong / Nginx)
* Core Business Service (Java, Spring Boot)
* Search Service (Elasticsearch)
* Database (PostgreSQL)
* Redis Cache (Redis)
  * Cache Data Store (Redis In-Memory Engine)
  * Eviction & TTL Manager
  * Connection & Command Router (Redis Cluster / Sentinel Interface)
* Notification Worker (Node.js)
* External Payment Gateway, Digital Content Providers / e-Book Vendors, Notification Service, External Enterprise Search Service (External Systems)

## Relationships
* Core Business Service -> Connection & Command Router: Routes read/write and TTL configuration commands via TCP/RESP (Pooled)
* Connection & Command Router -> Cache Data Store: Manages internal Redis memory operations
* Core Business Service -> Database: Queries persistent data via PostgreSQL protocol

## Technology Stack
* React & TypeScript: Powers the Web Application for responsive self-service portals
* Java & Spring Boot: Implements the Core Business Service for robust domain logic
* PostgreSQL: Provides reliable relational storage respecting EU-only data residency
* Elasticsearch: Delivers high-performance search to meet the <800ms NFR
* Redis: Accelerates access and reduces database load via in-memory caching

## Rationale
This architecture uses an in-memory caching layer with connection pooling to satisfy high-concurrency performance requirements. It strictly maintains data residency constraints by keeping sensitive processing and volatile session data within compliant boundaries.

    destination: "Cache Data Store"
    description: "Manages internal Redis memory operations"

Notification Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Notification Worker is an asynchronous background component of the Library Management System responsible for decoupled notification processing. It ensures reliable, GDPR-compliant delivery of alerts to patrons and staff.

## Key Elements
* **Queue Consumer Component**: Node.js worker consuming background jobs.
* **Template Engine Component**: Handlebars-based rendering engine.
* **Compliance Sanitizer Component**: TypeScript-based PII masking engine.
* **Dispatcher Client Component**: Axios-based HTTP client.
* **Retry & Dead-Letter Handler Component**: Exception and backoff manager.

## Relationships
* Queue Consumer -> Template Engine: Passes raw event payloads [In-memory function call]
* Template Engine -> Compliance Sanitizer: Passes rendered payload [In-memory function call]
* Compliance Sanitizer -> Dispatcher Client: Sends sanitized payload [In-memory function call]
* Dispatcher Client -> Notification Service: Sends alerts [HTTPS]
* Queue Consumer -> Retry & DLQ: Handles processing exceptions [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
* **Node.js**: Lightweight runtime optimized for I/O-bound background processing.
* **amqplib**: AMQP protocol library for asynchronous queue consumption.
* **Handlebars**: Template engine for rendering localized messages.
* **Axios**: HTTP client for secure external dispatch.
* **TypeScript**: Provides type safety for compliance and PII sanitization.

## Rationale
This decoupled, event-driven architecture isolates the core domain from external delivery failures while ensuring strict adherence to EU data residency and privacy constraints.
